newsitem.title: UK: TransCo pays 15.46 pence a therm for weekend gas.
newsitem.headline: TransCo pays 15.46 pence a therm for weekend gas.

text.p: British Gas Plc's pipeline division TransCo, which operates Britain's trunk gas pipeline network, the National Transmission System (NTS), said on Monday that it had paid 15.46 pence a therm on the flexibility mechanism over the weekend.

A TransCo spokeswoman told Reuters that TransCo bought nine separate gas lots, totalling 101,539,824 kilowatt hours (around 3.465 million therms) on the gas day October 4, which runs from 0600 hours on October 4 to 0600 hours on October 5.
TransCo paid a System Average Price (SAP) of 0.5276 pence per kilowatt hour (15.4624 pence a therm) for the gas.
On the gas day of Saturday, October 5, TransCo sold 76,210,690 kilowatt hours (2.6 million therms) of gas at an SAP of 0.400 pence per kilowatt hour (11.7228 pence a therm).
There was no trade on the gas day of Sunday, October 6.
Under phase 2 of the Network Code, which sets out rules for all users of the NTS, gas shippers must balance their inputs and offtakes on a daily basis.
To facilitate this, the flexibility mechanism was introduced to allow TransCo, as operator, to buy from, or sell to, shippers at a price bid by the shippers in order to balance the system.
